neighbours.label: in music-theory text, the token right before an interval or chord-size word is due ('intervals of | thirds', 'octaves, fifths, and | fourths', '(a | triad)'): the model is about to name an interval
fire: The two flutes play the tune together in intervals of sixths and thirds.
Medieval singers doubled the chant in parallel octaves, fifths, and fourths.
The guitar is tuned mostly in intervals of fourths, with one major third.
The simplest chord has three notes stacked in thirds (a triad) and sounds stable.
The horns answer the theme with soft calls in intervals of fifths.
Barbershop harmony fills the space between the melody and the bass with stacked thirds.
A power chord contains only the root and the note an interval of a fifth above it.
The pedal makes each note sound again one octave higher, one lower, or both.
quiet: The two flutes play the tune together at a slow and gentle tempo.
Medieval singers performed the chant in stone chapels, cloisters, and halls.
The guitar is tuned mostly by ear, with one electronic tuner as a check.
The simplest song has three verses sung in turn (a ballad) and sounds familiar.
The horns answer the theme with soft calls in the key of D minor.
Barbershop quartets fill the hall between the first act and the last with comic songs.
The street lamps stand along the avenue at intervals of fifty metres.
The pedal makes each note sound again a little louder, a little softer, or both.

short: about to name a musical interval
notes: Card: peaks on ' of', 'a', ' and', ' one', ',' right before fourths / fifths / triad / octave; the + direction suppresses ' perfect', ' fourth', ' third', ' fifth', ' octave', so this pole promotes them. The + pole is the neighbouring distinction: about to name a key or mode (major and | minor, 'in the key of'; promotes ' key', ' mod'). Probes: 'intervals of thirds' 1.20, 'tuned in ... fourths' 0.66, 'called a triad' 0.64, 'up an octave' 0.12; key / tempo / 'intervals of ten feet' < 0.10.
